newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia money market brisker, eyes intervention.
newsitem.headline: Croatia money market brisker, eyes intervention.

text.p: Croatia's money market trade picked up on Friday amid stronger end-of-week demand for kuna funds while borrowers also repaid previous loans, dealers said.
"The market has seen quite a high demand, but liquidity is not overstrained," a dealer told Reuters.
Fresh trade rose considerably to 48.1 million kuna, but still left some 20 million available on the supply side.
Call money accounted for 38.6 million kuna of the total and was granted at an unchanged 11 percent-rate. The rest were term loans at an unchanged 13-15 percent.
Banks were busy repaying 22 million kuna in previous loans in expectation of a central bank intervention through an injection of repo funds later today.
Thursday's overnight trade totalled 10 million as one bank sought to maintain its mandatory reserve. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
